atoms.name: Distance vector idea
atoms.one_line: Each router keeps a vector of costs to all destinations and sends it only to neighbours. Update is Bellman-Ford.

atoms.name: Updating a vector from neighbours
atoms.one_line: New cost to t is the minimum over neighbours v of c(x,v) plus v's advertised cost to t; the arg-min is the next hop.

atoms.name: Rounds and convergence
atoms.one_line: Info moves one hop per round. Good news (cost drop) spreads fast; bad news (failure) spreads slowly.

atoms.name: Count-to-infinity and fixes
atoms.one_line: After a failure two routers feed each other stale routes and costs climb. Split horizon, poison reverse, and a small infinity (RIP 16) limit it.

atoms.name: Link-state flooding
atoms.one_line: Each router floods its neighbour costs to everyone; all routers end with the same map. Flooding one LSA costs 2E-(V-1) transmissions.

atoms.name: Dijkstra at a router
atoms.one_line: Grow a tree from the source by settling the nearest unsettled node; the first hop of each tree path is the forwarding entry.

atoms.name: DV versus LS and protocols
atoms.one_line: LS: whole map, Dijkstra, faster convergence, more computation, transient loops. DV: neighbours only, loops can persist. RIP is DV (hop count), OSPF is LS.
